user.description: Choose a pvvx sensor to update.

bluetooth_confirm.description: Add {name}? This connects once over Bluetooth to confirm it runs pvvx firmware and to read its board and version.

pin.title: PIN needed (experimental)
pin.description: {name} has a PIN and no proxy has paired with it yet. Enter the PIN: Home Assistant hands it to a Bluetooth proxy that offers the pairing action (the proxy pairs with the sensor and keeps the bond). This takes about 25 seconds. The PIN is stored in this entry so that pairing can be repeated if the proxy loses the bond.

reauth_confirm.title: PIN needed again
reauth_confirm.description: {name} refuses the link and no PIN is stored for it (or the stored one no longer works), so its pairing with the Bluetooth proxy was lost. Enter the PIN: Home Assistant hands it to a proxy that offers the pairing action, which pairs with the sensor again. This takes about 25 seconds.

reconfigure.title: Store the PIN
reconfigure.description: Store the PIN of {name} so that Home Assistant can pair it again by itself if the proxy loses the pairing. Pairing is repeated through a proxy that offers the pairing action now; this takes about 25 seconds.

abort.not_pvvx: This device did not answer like pvvx custom firmware (it may be a different BTHome device or ATC1441 firmware).
abort.pin_protected: This sensor has a PIN set and no proxy can pair it (no ESPHome proxy that hears it offers the pair_pvvx action, and none has a bond with it), so it was not added and is now ignored so that it is not offered again. Add the pairing package to a proxy (see docs/pin-sensors.md in the integration repository), then un-ignore it on the integration page (Ignored devices). Or remove the PIN in TelinkMiFlasher.
abort.pin_protected_manual: This sensor has a PIN set and no proxy can pair it (no ESPHome proxy that hears it offers the pair_pvvx action, and none has a bond with it), so it was not added. Add the pairing package to a proxy (see docs/pin-sensors.md in the integration repository) and try again, or remove the PIN in TelinkMiFlasher.
abort.reauth_successful: The PIN was stored and the sensor is paired again.
abort.no_pin_sensor: This sensor has no PIN pairing; there is nothing to configure.

error.cannot_connect: Could not connect to the sensor (this is not a PIN problem: the connection itself did not complete within about 25 seconds). pvvx sensors are connectable only part of the time; a weak signal or a busy proxy also causes this. Wait a minute and try again.
error.unexpected: Unexpected error: {error}. See the Home Assistant log (pvvx_ota) for the traceback.
error.pin_wrong: The proxy paired with the PIN, but {name} still refuses the connection. This is a problem on the sensor, usually an old pairing entry or old firmware. Fix it once with TelinkMiFlasher ({flasher_url}) near the sensor: 1) connect and update the firmware to the latest version, 2) set the PIN to 0 and save, then set your PIN again (this clears the sensor's pairing memory), 3) add the sensor here again.
error.no_pairing_proxy: No proxy that hears this sensor offers the pairing action any more. See docs/pin-sensors.md in the integration repository.
error.pair_connect_failed: The proxy could not connect to the sensor to pair it (pvvx sensors are connectable only part of the time). Try again in a moment.
error.pair_no_passkey: {name} paired without asking for the PIN and still refuses the connection. This is a problem on the sensor, usually an old pairing entry or old firmware. Fix it once with TelinkMiFlasher ({flasher_url}) near the sensor: 1) connect and update the firmware to the latest version, 2) set the PIN to 0 and save, then set your PIN again (this clears the sensor's pairing memory), 3) add the sensor here again.

progress.pairing: Pairing {name} through its proxy and checking it. This takes about 30 to 40 seconds.

flash_file.name: Flash local firmware file
flash_file.description: Flashes a firmware image from a local file. The file name must be BOARD_vNN.bin matching the device's board.

path.name: Path
path.description: Path to the .bin file (must be inside an allowed directory).

force.name: Force
force.description: Flash even if the battery voltage is below 2.5 V (or unknown low).

flash_latest.name: Flash latest release
flash_latest.description: Flashes the latest release image for this sensor even if it is up to date. Used to tune the flash speed.

status_every.name: Status interval
status_every.description: Blocks between status reads (default 8). Larger is faster if the sensor and proxy keep up; too large makes lost blocks abort the flash.

force.name: Force
force.description: Flash even if the battery voltage is below 2.5 V (or unknown low).

set_encryption.name: Set advert encryption
set_encryption.description: Switches encrypted adverts on or off. Switching on stores a key in the sensor (generated if you give none) and returns it in the response only. Home Assistant's BTHome entry for the sensor needs that key afterwards (this integration does not change it) or the sensor's data is lost to HA.

key.name: Key
key.description: Optional 32 hex characters (16 bytes). Generated if empty.

set_pin.name: Set PIN
set_pin.description: WARNING: setting a PIN erases the sensor's bonds, and a sensor with a PIN only answers over an encrypted link. Without a proxy that holds a bond for it (see docs/pin-sensors.md) Home Assistant can no longer connect to it; TelinkMiFlasher can remove the PIN. 0 turns the PIN off. This integration neither logs nor stores it (the action call itself passes through Home Assistant's event bus, see docs/pin-sensors.md).

confirm.name: Confirm
confirm.description: Must be true; otherwise the action refuses.

update_entity_not_ready.message: The firmware update entity is not ready yet.

paired_proxy_does_not_see_sensor.message: {name} is not reachable via the paired proxy ({proxy}): it does not see the sensor right now. A PIN sensor only answers through the proxy that holds its bond, so no connection was made. Try again later or move that proxy closer to the sensor.

connected_via_wrong_proxy.message: {name} is not reachable via the paired proxy ({proxy}): the connection went through {link}. A PIN sensor only answers through the proxy that holds its bond, so nothing was sent. Try again later or move that proxy closer to the sensor.

proxy_not_verifiable.message: {name}: this Home Assistant version does not say which proxy the connection runs through, so it cannot be checked against the paired proxy ({proxy}). Nothing was sent to the sensor.

not_connectable.message: {name} ({address}) is not connectable right now: {reason}. pvvx sensors are connectable only part of the time; try again in a minute.

connect_timeout.message: Could not connect to {name} ({address}) within {seconds} s: {reason}. This is not a PIN problem: the sensor did not accept a connection. A weak signal or a busy proxy can cause this; try again or move a proxy closer.

pair_call_failed.message: Could not call the pairing action of {proxy}: {error}

pair_connect_failed.message: {proxy} could not connect to {address} to pair it. pvvx sensors are connectable only part of the time; try again.

unrecognised_reply.message: {name}: the reply to the version request was not recognised. Is this pvvx custom firmware?

path_not_allowed.message: {path} is not in an allowed directory. Add its folder to allowlist_external_dirs in the Home Assistant configuration.

battery_low.message: {name}: the battery is at {volts} V, below the limit of {limit} V. Replace the battery first, or call the action again with force: true.

queue_timeout.message: {name}: waited more than {hours} h for the earlier firmware operations.

pin_needs_confirmation.message: Refused: with a PIN set, Home Assistant and its proxies can no longer connect to the sensor unless a proxy holds a bond for it; only TelinkMiFlasher can remove the PIN. Call again with confirm: true if you really want this.

flash_running.message: A firmware flash is running. Try again when it has finished.

value_mismatch.message: {name}: the sensor stored {stored} instead of the requested {requested}.

nothing_to_restore.message: There are no saved settings to restore.

encryption_key_gone.message: The sensor holds no encryption key any more.

encryption_not_switched_on.message: {name}: the sensor did not switch encryption on. The new key was stored; run the action again.

encryption_not_switched_off.message: {name}: the sensor did not switch encryption off.

bad_key.message: The key must be 32 hexadecimal characters (16 bytes).

key_not_accepted.message: {name}: the sensor did not accept the key. This board may not support encrypted advertisements.

bad_pin.message: The PIN must be 0 (turns it off) or up to 6 digits.

pin_not_stored.message: {name}: the sensor could not store the PIN.

reboot_not_confirmed.message: {name}: the sensor did not confirm the reboot command ({error}). Older firmware may not have it.

temperature_offset_mismatch.message: {name}: the sensor stored a temperature offset of {stored} instead of {requested}.

humidity_offset_mismatch.message: {name}: the sensor stored a humidity offset of {stored} instead of {requested}.

slope_changed.message: {name}: the sensor changed its slope factors. Check them with TelinkMiFlasher.

sensor_not_heard.message: {name} ({address}) has not been heard by a connectable Bluetooth scanner yet.

adv_type_changed.title: {name}: advertising type is not BTHome
adv_type_changed.description: The sensor no longer advertises in BTHome format, so Home Assistant's BTHome integration stops receiving its data. Set the advertising type back to BTHome (the entity is disabled by default; enable it) or via TelinkMiFlasher.

encryption_changed.title: {name}: advert encryption changed
encryption_changed.description: Encryption of the sensor's adverts was switched. Home Assistant's BTHome entry for this sensor must have the matching bindkey (or none when encryption is off), otherwise its data is lost. This integration does not change that entry.

pin_bond_lost.title: {name}: pairing lost, pair again from the proxy
pin_bond_lost.description: This sensor has a PIN and was added with a bond stored in one ESPHome proxy, but it now refuses the link even after encryption. The proxy probably lost the bond (flash erase, NVS wipe) or the PIN was changed. Press the pair button on the proxy again (see docs/pin-sensors.md in the integration repository); this issue clears after the next successful read.

pin_set.title: {name}: a PIN was set
pin_set.description: A PIN was set on this sensor, so it only answers over an encrypted link and Home Assistant can no longer read it. Pair it through an ESPHome proxy with the pairing package (see docs/pin-sensors.md, then Reconfigure the entry), or remove the PIN in TelinkMiFlasher.

pin_pairing_failed.title: {name}: could not be paired with its PIN
pin_pairing_failed.description: The proxy paired with the PIN, but the sensor ({address}) still refuses the connection, so it was not added. This is a problem on the sensor, usually an old pairing entry or old firmware. Fix it once with TelinkMiFlasher ({flasher_url}) near the sensor: 1) connect and update the firmware to the latest version, 2) set the PIN to 0 and save, then set your PIN again (this clears the sensor's pairing memory), 3) add the sensor here again. This notice disappears when the sensor has been added.

reset_defaults.title: {name}: settings were reset to defaults
reset_defaults.description: The sensor's configuration was reset. Advertising type and encryption may differ from before, so check Home Assistant's BTHome entry. The previous settings can be written back with the 'Restore previous settings' button (not the encryption flag).

encryption_restore_failed.title: {name}: encryption was not switched back on
encryption_restore_failed.description: The flash cleared the sensor's BTHome encryption flag and it could not be switched on again automatically (the sensor may no longer hold the key). Until then Home Assistant's BTHome entry, which has the key, cannot read the sensor. Use the pvvx_ota.set_encryption action with your existing key (Developer tools > Actions) to switch it on again.

settings_differ_after_flash.title: {name}: settings differ from before the flash
settings_differ_after_flash.description: The flash changed some of the sensor's settings. They are not re-applied automatically: press 'Restore previous settings' on the sensor's device page if you want them back.

flash_failed.title: {name}: firmware update failed
flash_failed.description: The last firmware operation on this sensor failed: {error}. The sensor keeps running its old firmware (a failed transfer is not applied). Move a Bluetooth proxy closer, check the sensor's battery and try again; the issue clears itself after the next successful flash.

flash_unconfirmed.title: {name}: flash may not have been applied
flash_unconfirmed.description: The firmware was sent, but the new version could not be read back afterwards, so it is not known whether the flash was applied. The installed version shown may be out of date. Check that the sensor advertises again (a battery pull restarts it), then press Refresh; the issue clears itself when the sensor answers with the new version.

data.min_battery_v: Minimum battery voltage for a flash
data.auto_restore_encryption: Switch BTHome encryption back on after a flash
data.device_poll_interval: How often to read the sensor's version

data_description.min_battery_v: A flash is refused below this voltage (flash_latest and flash_file can override it with force).
data_description.auto_clock_sync: Check the sensor's clock in connections made anyway and set it if it is more than 5 s off.
data_description.auto_restore_encryption: A flash clears the encryption flag; if it was on, it is switched on again (the key stays on the sensor).
data_description.device_poll_interval: A Bluetooth connection per sensor. The firmware list and update offers are refreshed separately (every 12 hours, no Bluetooth), and a flash or the Refresh button read the sensor anyway.

options.never: Never (only on demand and after a flash)
